title: Store upgrades and licences
summary: Growing the shop is not only about floor space: Supermarket Simulator ties products and licences to a store level, so what you may sell grows with the shop.
body: Licences are their own objects in the game, which is why being allowed to sell something is a separate step from being able to afford it.
A product can carry a required store level, so the catalogue opens up as the shop grows instead of being available in one go.
Products keep their own identity, so an unlocked licence changes what you can order rather than what already sits on your shelf.
What this entry does not tell you: licence prices, the order the licences unlock in, or how much each upgrade costs. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Licences are separate objects in the game.
A product can require a minimum store level before it is available.
Products are tracked individually, so a licence changes what can be ordered.
The licence screen is built from its own product entries and a slider, with a set of licence materials behind it.
Licences are laid out as a row of their own, one model per licence, each with its own code of letters and digits.
facts.evidence: asset names: SM_license_us_Row, SM_license_us_N700, SM_license_us_WS15, SM_license_us_Su4

facts.claim: The licence screen names an information line, a name and an item for each licence, plus a separate item for downloadable content.
facts.evidence: asset names: License Info, License Name, License Item, License Item DLC
